findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "sitemap" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Sitemap parser: reads one public XML sitemap or sitemap index as structured URLs and source-reported dates. Supports gzip, substring filtering and pagination. L…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "web" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, pack_web_research, news, pack_news_sentiment, contents, image_metadata, extract, extract_rendered, pdf_text, sitemap, summarize, screenshot, papers, feed, url_meta, robots, url_redirects, url_uptime, seo_audit · Private data: url_favicon, pdf_text, url_redirects · Public sink: image_metadata · Destructive: image_metadata, summarize.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, pack_web_research, news, pack_news_sentiment, contents, image_metadata, extract, extract_rendered, pdf_text, sitemap, summarize, screenshot, papers, feed, url_meta, robots, url_redirects, url_uptime, seo_audit · Private data: url_favicon, pdf_text, url_redirects · Public sink: image_metadata · Destructive: image_metadata, summarize

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "news" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
